A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SeTGAP research. Full text extraction and visual inspection cover the main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–K, supporting reliable comparison despite renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: V3 reports original synthetic and Feynman experiments, noise tests, ablations, runtime measurements, and variable-ordering analyses in Section 4 and the appendices.

after.justification: V4 retains these original empirical results, including benchmark comparisons and appendix analyses. Its additional adaptive-sampling example is explicitly attributed to prior work.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1–4, the Multi-Set Transformer, skeleton selection and merging, and coefficient optimization remain unchanged. The adaptive-sampling example illustrates use of the existing method without revising SeTGAP's procedure.

E1.justification: Section 4.1 newly includes a prior-work example involving an incomplete, heteroskedastic dataset for 10 + 5 cos(x²/5), progressively augmented through adaptive sampling. This adds a distinct data-acquisition scenario; the 13 synthetic problems, four SRBench++ functions, and 78 selected Feynman problems remain unchanged.

E2.justification: The evaluated comparator sets remain unchanged in both the synthetic and Feynman comparisons. ScaleSR is newly discussed but explicitly excluded from evaluation; ASPINN supplies samples in the added example rather than serving as a competing SR method.

E3.justification: The newly included adaptive-sampling example uses ASPINN to add five samples per iteration and reports whole-domain MSE at iterations 1, 5, 10, through 50. Existing benchmark data generation, model settings, evaluation metrics, and extrapolation procedures are unchanged.

E4.justification: V4 adds an adaptive-sampling case study examining recovery under changing epistemic uncertainty. Appendix H adds finer computational-cost analysis, and Appendix K expands its existing ordering analysis with an intermediate failure trace. The original ablations and noise tests are retained.

E5.justification: Repeated-run and seed descriptions, standard deviations and standard errors, and Tukey HSD and Kruskal–Wallis/Dunn–Holm procedures are retained. The added adaptive-sampling example reports iteration-specific fits and MSE without introducing a new uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Appendix K revises all four I.50.26 final expressions and MSE values: for ordering [x0,x3,x1,x2], MSE changes from 1.41 in v3 Table 51 to 0.5768 in v4 Table 53. V4 also adds adaptive-sampling results and resource measurements. The principal benchmark results remain unchanged; the PDFs do not establish that the revised ordering results came from reruns.

T1.justification: Definition 1, Proposition 1, its Appendix C proof, and the mathematical objectives remain unchanged. The new notation table summarizes existing mathematics, while the ScaleSR projection example provides conceptual explanation rather than a new formal result.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims concerning decomposable surrogate extraction, functional-form recovery, noise robustness, and competitive Feynman performance.

C2.justification: V4 adds an argument about comparison fairness when the surrogate learns from the same fixed dataset, discusses projection and error-propagation issues relative to ScaleSR, and interprets unstable early discoveries during adaptive sampling. Appendix H additionally explains how coefficient counts affect optimization cost.

D1.justification: V4 adds a code-access link on page 1. Appendix H newly reports approximately 1.47 seconds, 392 GFLOPs, and 149.47 MB peak memory per skeleton candidate, along with sequential inference and cumulative-cost details. Existing hardware and stage-runtime disclosures remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V4 adds references to ScaleSR and ASPINN and a focused comparison with ScaleSR in Section 3.4.2. The existing CVGP comparison moves into Section 3.4.1, while the previously cited 2026 work receives expanded application discussion.

P1.justification: The title changes from 'Neuro' to 'Neural.' V4 adds a Section 3.3 roadmap, creates Section 3.4 for decomposition-method comparisons, and expands explanatory passages. Most existing prose and the overall document organization remain intact.

P2.justification: V4 adds notation Table 1, adaptive-sampling Table 9 and Figure 3, and failure-trace Figure 9. Existing figure images are unchanged, with several figures, algorithms, and tables relocated or renumbered within the retained layout.

improvement.justification: The notation guide, clearer method comparisons, code pointer, and finer resource disclosures improve readability and reproducibility information. The adaptive-sampling example and failure trace help readers assess behavior under imperfect surrogate models, although the sampling results are attributed to prior work. These are limited gains; the central method and principal benchmark evidence remain unchanged.
